Let <MATH_0001> be an immersion of algebraic stacks.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is locally Noetherian, then
<MATH_0003> is locally Noetherian and <MATH_0004> is quasi-compact.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0005> is Noetherian, then <MATH_0006> is Noetherian.
<STRUCT_0004>

Choose a scheme <MATH_0001> and a surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0002>.
Then <MATH_0003> is a scheme and
<MATH_0004> is an immersion, see
Properties of Stacks, Definition <REF_0001>.
Recall that <MATH_0005> is locally Noetherian if and only if <MATH_0006>
is locally Noetherian. In this case <MATH_0007> is locally Noetherian too
(Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0002> and
<REF_0003>) and <MATH_0008> is quasi-compact
(Properties, Lemma <REF_0004>).
This shows that <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact
(Lemma <REF_0005>)
and that <MATH_0010> is locally Noetherian.
Finally, if <MATH_0011> is Noetherian, then we see from the above
that <MATH_0012> is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian.
To finish the proof observe that <MATH_0013> is separated and hence
<MATH_0014> is quasi-separated because <MATH_0015> is so by
Lemma <REF_0006>.

Let <MATH_0001> be an algebraic stack.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is locally Noetherian then <MATH_0003>
is a locally Noetherian topological space.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0004> is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, then
<MATH_0005> is a Noetherian topological space.
<STRUCT_0004>

Assume <MATH_0001> is locally Noetherian.
Choose a scheme <MATH_0002> and a surjective smooth morphism
<MATH_0003>. As <MATH_0004> is locally Noetherian
we see that <MATH_0005> is locally Noetherian. By
Properties, Lemma <REF_0001>
this means that <MATH_0006> is a locally Noetherian topological space.
Since <MATH_0007> is open and surjective we conclude that
<MATH_0008> is locally Noetherian by
Topology, Lemma <REF_0002>.
This proves (1). If <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian,
then <MATH_0010> is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Hence
<MATH_0011> is Noetherian by Topology, Lemma
<REF_0003>.
